scope: Disposable SQLite transaction/lifecycle tests and mocked Supabase transport; no physical hardware or remote mutation.
command: python -c "import sys; sys.modules['readline']=None; import pytest; raise SystemExit(pytest.main(['tests/test_analysis_reliability.py','tests/test_cloud_analysis_reliability.py','tests/test_hardware_provenance.py','tests/test_recovery.py','tests/test_cloud.py','-q','--tb=short']))"

backlog_case.note: Older jobs are explicitly superseded by the newest admitted frame; this is not a claim of retrospective modelling of 153 observations.

verified_behaviors: Durable capped failure backoff does not starve newer ready jobs.
Partial result/event writes roll back on computation failure or expired lease.
Eight competing local threads commit one job outcome.
Expired ownership is reclaimable; active ownership is skipped.
An old device job cannot relabel a replacement device's acquisition that reuses its boot and sequence identity.
Read and write outages back off without ending the continuous worker.
Shutdown wakes a sleeping worker and waits only for its current job before stopping a batch.
The actual application lifespan starts and stops recovery; diagnostics require operator authorization.
Mock-cloud CAS rejects competing claims and stale outcomes atomically.
Durable cloud queue commits survive an outer HTTP-unit-of-work rollback.
Physical decisions and their events record explicit analyzer and rule versions.
limits: Supabase tests use mock HTTP transport, not an operational deployed database.
No fleet-capacity, live hardware or electrical protection claim.
A lease expiry may allow repeated computation, while fencing prevents duplicate committed outcomes.
Local API throughput is measured separately by scripts/rehearse_api_performance.py.
